page: Vultr vbm-24c-256gb-amd is a bare metal server configured with an AMD EPYC 7443P processor. This x86_64 architecture CPU features 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.85 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 5.33 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 960 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this hardware configuration.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 10% at 3249.57. Multi-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% with a stress-ng multi-core score of 77709.84 and a PassMark CPU score of 60061.01. Memory performance is also highly rated, with the PassMark memory score reaching the top 10% at 3105.89, though uncached memory read and write bandwidth benchmarks fall into the middle 50% average tier. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates strong capabilities in cryptography and small-model LLM text generation, where it achieves top-tier throughput of 388.22 tokens per second.

As a bare metal instance with dedicated CPU allocation, this server offers high resource density and predictable performance without virtualization overhead. The combination of 48 dedicated threads, 256 GB of DDR4 RAM, and local SSD storage makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring sustained CPU and memory utilization. It is suited for database operations, multi-threaded decompression tasks, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference on small to medium models.
